title: Autoscaler telemetry contract and tenant safe-mode proposal
content:
Background:

Redwood Dedicated customers require predictable latency, but workloads vary and induce short-lived spikes. Current autoscaler behavior focuses on capacity allocation and basic alarms (utilization, queue length). We lack a standardized telemetry contract and a clear, operator-friendly safe-mode that can be enacted automatically or by SREs to preserve SLOs during volatility.

This doc proposes a minimal, backward-compatible telemetry contract (what the serving runtime and control plane must emit), plus a tenant 'safe-mode' state machine and an operator runbook. The goal is to let the autoscaler make conservative decisions when risk is high, and to give customers and operators transparent signals for fast mitigation.

Goals:
- Define a concise set of per-tenant and per-pool telemetry signals (ingest, emit frequency, semantics).
- Define tenant risk scoring and safe-mode arming levels so orchestrators can react predictably.
- Specify control-plane API hooks and fallback behaviors for graceful isolation and temporary throttles.
- Provide an operator playbook for diagnosing and intervening with minimal customer impact.

Non-goals:
- Not an exhaustive telemetry schema for all internal infra metrics (we focus on signals relevant to autoscaling and isolation).
- Not a full billing or chargeback spec (we reference existing billing pipelines).

Proposal overview:
1) Telemetry contract: canonical signals emitted at 5s or 1m resolution depending on metric. All signal names are dotted and namespaced (redwood.dedicated.<pool|tenant>.<metric>). Emit over existing telemetry pipeline (Prometheus/OTLP) and surface via control-plane for autoscaler decisions.

Required per-tenant signals (examples):
- redwood.dedicated.tenant.<tenant_id>.rps_incoming (int/sec) -- raw request arrival rate
- redwood.dedicated.tenant.<tenant_id>.tokens_consumed_rate (tokens/sec) -- billing token proxy for cost-aware decisions
- redwood.dedicated.tenant.<tenant_id>.p99_latency_ms (ms) -- tight SLO indicator
- redwood.dedicated.tenant.<tenant_id>.queued_requests (count) -- backlog size on serving nodes
- redwood.dedicated.tenant.<tenant_id>.kv_cache_hit_ratio (0..1) -- opportunity for cache-driven optimization
- redwood.dedicated.tenant.<tenant_id>.eviction_risk_score (0..100) -- derived risk (see scoring below)

Required per-pool signals:
- redwood.dedicated.pool.<pool_id>.gpu_utilization_pct (0..100)
- redwood.dedicated.pool.<pool_id>.slot_free_count (count)
- redwood.dedicated.pool.<pool_id>.pending_warmups (count)
- redwood.dedicated.pool.<pool_id>.preemptions_recent (count/5m)

Signal semantics and frequency:
- Core metrics (rps_incoming, p99_latency_ms, gpu_utilization_pct, queued_requests) should be emitted at 5s granularity with stable monotonic reset semantics.
- Derived/aggregates (eviction_risk_score, tokens_consumed_rate) may be emitted at 1m granularity.
- All metrics must include tenant_id/pool_id and optionally model_id and route_id.

Eviction risk scoring (one recommended formula):
- Risk components: latency_pressure (weighted p99 vs target), backlog_pressure (queued requests normalized by tenant concurrency), capacity_headroom (pool free slots normalized), recent_preemptions.
- ev_risk = clamp(0,100, 40*latency_pressure + 30*backlog_pressure + 20*(1-capacity_headroom) + 10*recent_preemptions)
- Interpretation: 0-30 low risk, 31-60 medium, 61-85 high, 86-100 critical.

Tenant safe-mode state machine:
States: NORMAL -> WATCH -> SOFT_SAFE -> HARD_SAFE -> RECOVERING
Triggers:
- NORMAL->WATCH: eviction_risk_score crosses 30 for > 30s
- WATCH->SOFT_SAFE: crosses 60 or queued_requests > threshold and p99>1.5x target
- SOFT_SAFE->HARD_SAFE: crosses 85 or sustained preemptions or pool-level thermal alerts
- Any safe mode enters operator-notify channel and optionally emails tenant contacts if configured

Soft-safe behavior (automated, low-customer-impact first):
- Enable prefix KV caching for tenant where advisable (best-effort)
- Short-duration rate-limits on new non-critical routes (configurable per-tenant route tag)
- Redirect/route lower-fidelity model variants for sampled requests (probabilistic fallback)
- Temporarily disable background heavy tasks (e.g., index updates) for the tenant

Hard-safe behavior (strong isolation):
- Enforce per-tenant concurrency ceilings (hard caps) at the gateway
- Evict best-effort or opportunistic slots allocated to the tenant in overcommit pools
- Fallback to pre-configured lower-cost model variants (with observability tagging)
- Route excess requests to queued rejections with clear reasons (429 with x-redwood-safe-mode header)

Control-plane APIs and handshake:
- GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/autoscale-status -> returns current state, risk_score, recent_reasons
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/safe-mode?action=arm|disarm|query -> operator can request manual arm/disarm; requires audit log entry and optional customer-notify flag
- Events: eventbus topic redwood.dedicated.safe_mode.{tenant_id} with JSON payloads (state, reason_codes, suggested_actions).
- Backward compatibility: if runtime cannot compute eviction_risk_score, fallback to a minimal heuristic (p99 and queued_requests) until runtime is upgraded.

Operator runbook (high level):
1) Alert: SAFE_MODE_ARMED (soft or hard) triggers SRE runbook page and Slack channel.
2) Verify telemetry: check p99, queued, evict_risk and pool headroom graphs (5m/1h window).
3) If soft-safe: enable caching hints and short-lived route throttles via control-plane UI. Document changes and notify tenant if they have opted in.
4) If hard-safe: escalate to incident and consider scaled evictions and rebalancing. Open a mitigation ticket and run pre-approved customer communication template.
5) Recovery: move from HARD_SAFE->RECOVERING when risk_score < 40 and sustained for 10m. Maintain increased monitoring for 1h.

Compatibility and migration plan:
- Phase 1 (Q4 2025): Emit new per-tenant metrics from serving-runtime with a runtime flag; produce a pilot with selected tenants.
- Phase 2 (Q1 2026): Add safe-mode state machine to control-plane; expose APIs and a UI panel.
- Phase 3 (Q2 2026): Automated actions (prefix-caching toggle, route throttles) kept behind feature flags; operator-only by default.

Metrics to judge success:
- Reduction in p99 SLO breaches during high-variance windows by X% (target 30% in pilot tenants).
- Mean time to safe-mode remediation (operator intervention or auto-recover) < 15m.
- Customer-reported incidents related to unexpected evictions drop by 50% for pilot tenants.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How do we avoid per-tenant metrics inflating cardinality in Prometheus? Proposed: export metrics with tenant label at a coarse rollup endpoint and push refined signals to control-plane only.
- What privacy/PII constraints exist for per-tenant telemetry? Need legal review for any customer contact and for storing tenant identifiers in long-term aggregates.
- Should safe-mode auto-notify tenants by default? Recommend opt-in during pilot.
- How do safe-mode actions interact with Dedicated billing and committed capacity guarantees? Billing/product need to review impact of enforced throttles vs customer expectations.

Implementation milestones (high level):
- 2025-10: Telemetry schema spec finalized; runtime team increments metric exports with feature flag.
- 2025-12: Control-plane ingest + risk-score service prototype; internal demo and operator feedback loop.
- 2026-02: Pilot with 3 customers, iterate on thresholds and actions.
- 2026-04: Roll out safe-mode UI and operator automation flags.

Appendix: sample alert template (Slack + email snippet)
- Subject: [DEDICATED][SAFE_MODE][tenant=acme-corp] Soft-safe triggered by high p99
- Body: Tenant acme-corp entered SOFT_SAFE at 2025-11-03T14:21Z. Key signals: p99=1420ms target=800ms; queued=320; evict_risk=72. Suggested first actions: enable prefix caching, apply temporary route throttle (route: /v2/generate non-critical=1).

Notes to reviewers:
- Please focus feedback on the eviction_risk formula, safe-mode thresholds, and operator UX requirements.
- Tag product-dedicated and eng-serving-runtime in comments.

End of doc.
